subject: Biological significance analysis using a single biological replicate

messages.author: a820f519b054088c
messages.subject: Biological significance analysis using a single biological replicate
parts:
Dear MSstats team,

I am using the Skyline tool for biological significance analysis using the group comparison feature and I noticed something unexpected to me: the TestingResult.csv file contains proteins which have data only for one biological replicate from within the two compared experimental conditions. They contain p-values and other statistics. I was surprised since I thought that MSstats will exclude such proteins from further statistical analysis since there is no information regarding their biological variability, and thus they are unsuitable for testing biological hypotheses. Please let me know if I have misunderstood something, and if there is a way to filter out those proteins from the result file.

Thank you very much in advance!

messages.author: df9ba0266a9a081f
messages.subject: Re: Biological significance analysis using a single biological replicate
parts:
I'm not 100% sure about your experimental design. But, generally, MSstats can test with one biological replicate, if there is any other technical replicate. Linear model will include only 'Group' term. If you use Skyline external tool, it is not easy to manipulate the data. What I have in mind is that you can uncheck the protein that has one biological replicate manually. If you use R, you can remove them easily.

Hope to help.

messages.author: a820f519b054088c
messages.subject: Re: Biological significance analysis using a single biological replicate
parts:
Thanks for the reply Meena!

My data does not have any technical replicates (multiple injections of the same sample), so maybe what you are saying is that linear models can use the variance between the selected features within a single biological replicate data (red box in attached figure) for its biological variance? I would normally assume you would have to derive biological variance from within data of biological replicates (green box). The figures shows 6 different experimental conditions, each had 4 biological replicates. As you can see, there is only one biological replicate for the right-most condition and I am wondering where does the variance for this condition come from to perform biological significance analysis.

I might have misunderstood something. I would appreciate if you could direct me towards some material to understand this better.

Thanks again!

messages.author: 085b00b73e467d88
messages.subject: Re: Biological significance analysis using a single biological replicate
parts: Equal-variance is assumed in the linear model, where all the replicates (in all conditions) are used for variance estimation.

messages.subject: Re: Biological significance analysis using a single biological replicate
parts:
Dear Meena,

As I am still having the same issue with another dataset, I would be very grateful if you could reply to my last post.

I hope you can also help me with the following. I went through the MSStats vignette and manual, but could not find how to constrain group comparisons in MSStats analysis in R with the following 1) only use proteins with biological replicates between the compared conditions (excluding proteins with data for one biological replicate); 2) only use proteins with data for more than 2 peptides in both compared conditions. 

2) is needed since even after filtering data with "Min 2 peptides per protein" in Skyline, some samples can still have data only for one peptide if only one of the samples has data for 2. I assume in this case, MSStats would still compare the samples, but I would like to constrain comparison only for proteins with at least 2 peptides for both compared conditions.

Thank you for your help!

messages.author: df9ba0266a9a081f
messages.subject: Re: Biological significance analysis using a single biological replicate
parts:
1) variance from biological replicate : In your profile plot, MSstats considers the variance in green, not red. There are 6 conditions and some conditions have biological replicate. When fitting linear model, MSstats use all conditions (not use only condition you assigned), in your case, use all 6 conditions. Then, MSstats calculate linear combination for assigned comparison. So, even though one condition has one biological replicate, MSstats can analyze.
  MSstats does not have option for 'only use proteins with biological replicates between the compared conditions'. If you want, you need to filter out before using MSstats.

2) I think 'Min 2 peptides per protein' in Skyline means that Skyline will report the proteins with minimum 2 peptides. But there is no restriction for Min 2 peptides per protein per condition or min 2 peptides per all MS runs, I guess.
 MSstats has similar option that remove protein with one peptide in all converter function (like SkylinetoMSstatsFormat). But, still it does not include the restriction 'per condition'. If you want to use the proteins with at least 2 peptides for both compared conditions, you need to filter out before your analysis.
